sponsor_or_proposer: TotalEnergies (Venus, PEL 56); TotalEnergies + Galp (Mopane, PEL 83) — no FLNG-specific developer/operator named yet
current_state: Conceptual only. Orange Basin oil discoveries (Venus, Mopane) carry very high associated-gas volumes; sponsors and the Namibian Gas Master Plan describe 'flexible monetization strategies including offshore FLNG solutions' alongside gas-to-power and reinjection. Upstream FIDs (Venus, Mopane) are targeted for 2026, but no separate FLNG facility has a named developer, a selected site/anchorage, a vessel, or any FLNG-specific concrete step (no FEED, MOU, or FID on a liquefaction/FLNG unit). Floating LNG is repeatedly described as 'being considered'/'being explored'.
missing_threshold_elements: Concrete step (no FLNG FEED/MOU/site selection — only upstream-development FIDs targeted); FLNG-specific sponsor/operator (the named companies are the upstream operators, not a committed FLNG developer); precise location/anchorage of any FLNG unit
watch_for: A dedicated FLNG developer/operator named for Orange Basin gas; an FLNG newbuild/conversion charter or shipyard order tied to Venus/Mopane; FEED award for a floating liquefaction unit; the Venus/Mopane FID(s) (targeted 2026) explicitly carving out an FLNG export stream rather than reinjection/gas-to-power. Re-check ~mid-2026 around the Venus FID window.
notes: Distinct from GEM's existing Walvis Bay LNG Terminal (T100000130622), which is an IMPORT/regas FSRU concept at Walvis Bay, not an offshore export FLNG. Also distinct from the Kudu gas field (BW Energy), whose current concept is gas-to-POWER near Luderitz via a floating production unit + pipeline + power plant (no LNG terminal — out of scope for this tracker). Independent non-GEM corroboration that FLNG is only an aspirational/'options being evaluated' monetization route for Orange Basin associated gas (no committed FLNG developer/site/FID): (1) worldoil 2026-01-30 (best_lead, PASS 'Venus') on the Venus/Mopane upstream FID trajectory; (2) Cliffe Dekker Hofmeyr oil&gas alert 2026-06-03 'Gas commercialisation: the missing link in Namibia's oil story' (https://www.cliffedekkerhofmeyr.com/en/news/publications/2026/Namibia/Oil-Gas/oil-and-gas-alert-3-june-Gas-commercialisation-The-missing-link-in-Namibias-oil-story) which lists FLNG among credible-but-unselected options (PASS 'FLNG'); (3) African Energy Chamber gas-master-plan writeup (https://energychamber.org/from-gas-master-plan-to-market-momentum-namibia-positions-natural-gas-at-the-center-of-energy-strategy/) naming FLNG export as one aspirational route (PASS 'Mopane'). Three independent non-GEM publishers; no gem.wiki citation. All url_verifier PASS (2026-06-04).
